content.value_statement: New endpoints can become inconsistent with Catalyst-Relay conventions. This skill guides route creation, validation, registration, response formatting, client mapping, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Creates endpoint files with colocated Zod request schemas, response types, and handler factories.
Registers Hono routes with the shared session manager.
Applies the established success and error response envelopes.
Maps HTTP functionality to ADTClient methods when library access is needed.
Produces endpoint documentation following the required project structure.
limitations: Applies specifically to the Catalyst-Relay repository structure and conventions.
Does not define authentication or authorization policy for new endpoints.
Does not implement unspecified core business logic.
Does not replace type checking, integration tests, or security review.

use_cases.title: Add a validated route
use_cases.description: Create a Hono handler with a colocated Zod schema and standard response envelope.

use_cases.title: Expose client functionality
use_cases.description: Wrap an existing core operation with an HTTP endpoint and matching ADTClient method.

use_cases.title: Document a new endpoint
use_cases.description: Prepare consistent request, response, error, use case, and library usage documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a {method} endpoint at {path} that returns {result}. Follow existing Catalyst-Relay route and response patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Add request validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create {path} with fields {fields}. Add Zod validation, typed responses, and clear validation errors.

prompt_templates.title: Map an endpoint to the client
prompt_templates.prompt: Expose {operation} through {method} {path}. Add the route, ADTClient method, and endpoint documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a complete endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement {endpoint} with validation, session handling, authorization checks, error mapping, client support, documentation, and relevant tests.

output_examples.input: Add a status endpoint that needs no request body.
output_examples.output: A registered status handler with a typed success response, standard error handling, and matching endpoint documentation.

output_examples.input: Expose package listing through the server and client library.
output: A validated packages route registered with the Hono application.
A matching ADTClient method for library users.
Documentation covering requests, responses, errors, and usage.

best_practices: Keep request schemas, response types, and handlers in the endpoint file.
Validate request data before invoking session or core functionality.
Run type checking and relevant tests after wiring routes and client methods.
anti_patterns: Do not return response shapes that bypass the standard success and error envelopes.
Do not accept request data without schema validation.
Do not add a route without registration and corresponding documentation.

faq.question: Which server framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Catalyst-Relay routes built with Hono and TypeScript.

faq.question: Where should a new route file be placed?
faq.answer: Place it under src/server/routes using the appropriate category and endpoint names.

faq.question: How are requests validated?
faq.answer: Define a colocated Zod schema and parse the request before running endpoint logic.

faq.question: When should ADTClient be updated?
faq.answer: Add a client method when the endpoint exposes core functionality needed in library mode.

faq.question: What response format should handlers use?
faq.answer: Use the project success envelope for data and the error envelope with a message, code, and status.

faq.question: Does the skill add tests automatically?
faq.answer: The source guidance requires type checking but does not specify a test pattern. Add relevant tests based on nearby endpoints.
